reasons: Rule correctly detected: the agreement contains no insurance covenant, yet Commerce One provides on-site professional services and hosts data (a services/hosting vendor), so an insert is the right remedy.

Inserted Section 14.10 tracks the playbook preferred position in full (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Corio/Customer data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) and is properly party-named for Commerce One as the vendor.

Placement in the Miscellaneous section with the existing 'Complete Understanding' clause renumbered 14.11 avoids a numbering collision and leaves all other text untouched (changed-character ratio 0.069 on p0133 reflects only the renumber).

Comment is accurate, cites the factual basis (on-site services and hosted MarketSite.net handling Corio and Customer data), states the playbook position, and offers the sanctioned fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) in the required tone.
